title: Not to be seen (Matthew 6:1–6)
hookLine: give, pray and fast in secret; your Father sees in secret

lines: WHO ARE YOU DOING IT FOR?
cards: Ever done something kind and felt the tiny itch to post about it? A donation, a volunteer shift, a good deed. Just a small photo, just so people know.
That pull is nothing new. Jesus turns to three practices of his people's faith: giving to the poor, praying and fasting. He doesn't say don't do them.
He assumes you will. He asks something sharper: who are you doing them for?

teach.b: Take heed, he says, that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them. Don't sound a trumpet when you give, the way the hypocrites do, to be praised.

Nobody's sure anyone literally blew trumpets; it may be a vivid picture, like blowing your own horn. Then, in the King James Bible: "But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth."
Give so quietly that even you half forget it. Hypocrite is worth opening.

teach.h: HUPOKRITES: AN ACTOR IN A MASK.
teach.b: In Greek, hupokrites meant a stage actor, someone who performed behind a mask. Jesus's point isn't about any one group. It's about anyone, in any faith or none, who performs goodness for an audience.

teach.h: THEY HAVE THEIR REWARD: PAID IN FULL.
teach.b: Three times he says of them: they have their reward. Scholars point out that the Greek verb turns up on ancient receipts: paid in full. They wanted applause, they got it, and that's the whole payment.
Then prayer: don't pray on street corners to be seen.
Instead: "But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which is in secret shall reward thee openly."
Closet here means an inner room, maybe a storeroom, the one room in a small house with a door.
It doesn't mean praying together is wrong; Luke says Jesus went to the synagogue on the sabbath, as his custom was, and he taught his friends a prayer that begins our Father. It's about the audience.
Fasting too: wash your face, look normal, let it be between you and God.

teach.h: THY FATHER WHICH IS IN SECRET.
teach.b: Thy Father which is in secret, he says, sees it. On his telling, the quiet good isn't wasted.

how: This passage is read in many churches on Ash Wednesday, at the start of Lent, when Christians take up quiet giving, prayer and fasting; some give anonymously and keep a private time of prayer each day.

games.q: you've just given a big gift to someone in need. a friend says: you should post about it, it'll inspire people. what does this passage point to?
o: let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.
games.why: give quietly: "let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth." the Father sees in secret.

practice: If you can, go into a room and shut the door: a bedroom, a bathroom, a parked car, anywhere with no audience, and notice what it's like to be unseen, with nobody to impress, nothing to perform.
If you pray, speak to God as simply as you'd speak to someone you trust. If you don't, just rest in the quiet, and let it be enough.

wordCard.voice: Hupokrites, the Greek word for a stage actor, someone who performs behind a mask. Give, pray and fast without an audience, because the Father sees in secret.

orig.note: Greek: actor, one who plays a part. English hypocrite comes from it.

carryVoice: Your line: the father sees in secret. No trumpet needed. Day two hundred forty-eight, quietly done.
